essence: By the stated rule all practice is established; the manifest support to grasp is the āgama.
As a worldly view, manifestation yields other fruit; rightly practiced, it yields Śiva.
The śāstra's own part is to be grasped; in small fruit its opposite is mostly accepted.
From the Khageśvarī state fearlessness removes poison; so from fearlessness comes the Bhairava state, karma destroyed.
The Ārṣa fall is explained in this left doctrine; quick accomplishment because all Ārṣa dwells in Māyā's womb.
All-knowing of whatever is seen is born of complete teaching; its fruit is supreme.
Lower principle is spoken lower, higher spoken higher; consciousness-accomplished is just so.
From the higher spoken, consciousness-accomplished is determined; the incomplete all-knower is known in lower doctrine.
Seeing the upper doctrine's part even in the abandoned, below in śāstras Māyā-nature is seen from creation and protection.
The venerable Ānanda-śāstra was first spoken by the Lord; Ṛṣi-words are much-suffering, unstable, small-fruited.
The scholar should not validate that; he should take refuge in the Śaiva āgama, explained by the Ārṣa fall in the left doctrine.
For quick accomplishment, all Ārṣa sits in Māyā's womb; from Khageśvarī fearlessness removes poison.
So karma is destroyed and the Bhairava state comes; ignorance of non-teaching is bitten in lower doctrine.
Its opposite must be grasped: the Śiva doctrine, in two attainments — Śrīkaṇṭha and Lakuleśvara.
Two streams make this śāstra non-Māyā, giving the final good; the eastern gives enjoyment as desired.
That fivefold śakti-variety is painted; five streams are spoken in Śrīkaṇṭha's doctrine.
Ten, eighteen-fold, five streams; the superior Bhairava is divided sixty-four.
The venerable Ānanda-śāstra was first spoken by the Lord; its pīṭha-collection is twofold, right and left.
Mantra, vidyā, and from them mudrā and maṇḍala; manana-protection-giving is called mantra, there by vidyā.
Support and nourishment are its meaning; mantra's counterpart mudrā causes nourishing.
Maṇḍala's essence is spoken: by hearing maṇḍa comes Śiva's name; thus the four pīṭhas' mutual mixture.
From that all becomes in pīṭha after pīṭha; in reality difference arises from that principality.
For sādhaka-lords' manifestation: each is fourfold — maṇḍala, mudrikā.
Mantra, vidyā, pīṭha — superior, higher, highest; vidyā-pīṭha is principal, per Siddhayogīśvarī.
Its supreme essence is the Mālinīvijayottara; so in Ratnamālā, by the Lord.
The complete tantra-essence depends on left and right; united as one Kaula in Śaḍardhaka.
Siddhānta has abundant action, defiled by mala and Māyā; right is fierce action, left is abundant siddhi.
Small merit, much suffering, void of own experience; void of liberation-vidyā and humility — abandon it far.
At that time, by the guru without thought, it is manifested; one is liberated by time, the machine simply stands.
I have fixed the streams' form from the supreme word; detail is spoken in the Mālinī-śloka-vārtika.
One desirous of knowing should ascertain this; we do not prize fruitless repetition.
Thus effortless living-liberation gives great fruit; as desired, great enjoyment is established.
Six-and-a-half essence of true śāstra is to be accepted; born by thirty-six principles, this Brahmāṇḍa is delightful yet various.
Seven cities from earth up are full; where else is the second world's happiness? Sun, moon, day, night spread enjoyment.
There three heavens' great enjoyment, precious islands, excess; Kumārikā rises place after place up to Śiva.
The paśu enjoying former karma fits enjoyment by birth; in one happy place he attains satisfaction of the supreme.
In Kanyā here is a greater place; where the best śāstras' eye is not born blind — who would blame the collyrium?
The complete śāstra's abode is the Middle Country; there a twice-born, Atrigupta, born excelling, rose by chewing the śāstra-ocean.
King Lalitāditya brought him to his city; from love he dwelt at the Himalaya's head, where Gaurī's lover wins all.
Sages made dwellings place by place; everywhere he, Candracūḍa, accomplishes all desired siddhi.
Where Śāradā shines, known as Śrī Śāradā; Śāṇḍilya's service pleases all by its glories.
Orange, pale, white, gold, dark radiances bloom; Kuntala, Kandalī resemble them, shining.
Three-eyed wrath's flame dissolves here; Kāma's arrows bloom by wine's pretext; attachment and love-fever act.
Lovers' speech grants pride; in embrace fear shakes off; all deities' radiance blossoms and wine spreads.
White shoots bloom, dark-red, deep-red filaments; scattered over earth where Kashmir's flowers please the goddess.
All the world is poet or scholar, hero or eloquent; moon-radiant citizens; suṣumnā swallows sun, moon, sky.
The supreme Pravara city was made by Pravarasena; at his end he released Maheśvara worship, sky-rising.
By swinging sounds the charming hero; his good conduct is proclaimed; conduct's essence, heavy radiant forms.
Full-moon pure radiance, deep-limbed saffron glory; the waved creeper's chowrie-flood gives royal abhiṣeka to Kāma.
At the established Maheśvara liṅga he smears scent and flowers; the sage-siddha, venerable, destroys sin.
Enjoyment and liberation complete the kalpa-vine; enjoyment alone gives taste; Hara's bow-art descends by the Vitastā.
Going to Kuvera's city, seen face-to-face with the moon-crest, he grew pure; dwelling on the Vitastā's bank he became king.
In his lineage Varāhagupta became Bhagavān; at death the god's ocean-wave touched his head, granting supreme grace.
His son Cukhulaka, moon-white intellect, Narasiṃhagupta; Māheśvarī devotion adorns his pure mind steeped in all śāstra.
Removing youth's burden, mounting renunciation's boat, by devotion's ascent he crushes the gems of doubt.
His son Abhinavagupta, purified by Candracūḍa's foot-pollen; his mother removed him in childhood; fate purifies by future rite.
His mother, supreme relative, thus speaks; affection intensifies bonds; in the root bond dissolved, I think, is the living one's liberation.
By his father he entered the word-jungle and logic-ocean; his mind purified, devoted to literature's dense taste, by Maheśa's devotion, taken by self-grasping pride.
Identified, he regarded no worldly practice; only to increase enjoyment he serves in the guru's houses.
Helmsman of the great ocean of bliss-continuity; with Kavarātmaja Vāmanātha, Śrīnātha, Śrībhūti by father's grace.
Traiyambaka, Somānanda's son Utpala, Jalakṣmaṇagupta, Turyā, Śrīsoma — all-knower Śaṃbhunātha.
Śrī Candraśarma, Yogānanda, Abhinanda, Śiva-Śakti and various nāthas; Dharmaśiva, Vāmanaka, Udbhaṭa, Bhāskara, headed great.
By serving these, grace matures; the śāstra-essence's auspicious domain is manifest in him; though people saw no field, he sees beings.
Then to grace, Śāṃbhava-devotion-holder, his brother full of śāstra-reflection; as much as his mind applies, so many worship him, though few.
Śrī Śauri's son Karṇa, knowing in youth the Śāṃbhava principle; abandoning the body, he proclaims truth to people, fallen from yoga to the great sage.
His childhood friend, the minister's son Śrīmandra, delightful in all essence; Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī made a pair; the co-wife removes auspicious power.
Others, paternal uncle's sons — Śiva, Śakti, Kṣema, Utpala, Abhinava, Cakraka, Padmagupta — who counted wealth as grass, hearts filled with Śambhu-service.
In six-and-a-half śāstras all mastered; Rāmagupta devoted to rite and maṇḍala, complete in the guru's service.
Another person, dependent on Śiva's śaktipāta, purpose by own śakti; averse to entreaty, untaught, yet grace is done to this group too.
He entreats the Ācārya intensely for complete tantra-attainment; divinely graced intellect is rightly born; wealth is one taste.
He agreed; desiring to dance he descended; grace inclined, by good gurus' command and auspicious birth.
Desiring to remove the scattered state, he chose residence in his own best city; even a child cowherd practices Maheśvara-service there.
By the creator his paternal uncle's wife became; she who dissolves saṃsāra's various thought; the cool moon-crest foot-pollen is her only ornament, Vatsalikā, fitting.
Embodied patience, like compassion, took body; support like good character's form; renunciation's essence ripened; the principle-meaning jewel shines.
Her brother too, by the moon-crest devotion, supreme purified-mind activity; Śauri accepted the Īśvara-minister state, abandoning king-minister state.
His daughter-in-law, Karṇa's wife, shaken by saṃsāra; she bore one son, named Yogeśvarī, fitting and shining in meaning.
In youth, distressed by husband-separation, she pitied; the three-eyed by devotion draws to me the future glory's rays.
Devotion blossoms with horripilation, clear limb-ornament; bowing to Śrī Śaṃbhunātha, forehead-marked; the Śaiva scripture is her ear-ornament.
Called Ambā, she saw the guru, her brother; by Śambhu's view, future glory radiant, good intellect; she knows truth not by relative thought.
His brother Abhinava too, not by name only but by true conduct and by knowledge-taste; his thirst grows greatly.
The other, destroying contraction's heart-lotus by Śāṃbhava rays, composed radiant glory; Lumpaka attends him with saintly effort.
Thus in Vatsalikā's house, concentrated in mind, having heard before and considered by own intellect, he obtained the śāstras' essence.
He made that composition of great meaning; by reason the āgama is spoken as tantra-principle; attaining light, this world moves happily.
May saints grace his work; may this first rule hold so long; then may she take your mind; may grace instantly by the principle's view.
Abhinavagupta composed this śāstra-essence; Śiva, listen so long; all ears praise your tantra; may Abhinava please the world by discussion of your form.

rasa.dominant: śānta (tranquility) with adbhuta weight (the finale: value of the teaching and its origin)
rasa.justification: The ahnika closes the Tantraloka: value of the teaching, its origin, the lineage, and the author; tranquility rests in the completed work.

sections.SUMMARY: The finale āhnika closes the Tantrāloka: value of the teaching, its origin, the Kashmir lineage, and the author; the work is offered to Śiva.
